bib.title: Learning to Filter Context for Retrieval-Augmented Generation

read.skipped: reference list skimmed only; no appendix in the PDF

question: Can training a sentence-level context filter before generation improve retrieval-augmented generation by removing irrelevant and distracting retrieved content?
hypothesis: The generator does better when grounded on precisely supporting content: removing distracting content from positive passages and removing negative passages improves output.
contributions: FILCO: sentence-wise context filtering trained on silver spans chosen by STRINC, LEXICAL or CXMI
Evaluation on six knowledge-intensive tasks with FLAN-T5 and LLAMA2
Analysis of which filtering measure suits which task

method.summary: Retrieved passages are split into sentences; a single best sentence is chosen as silver context using a task-specific measure (string inclusion, unigram F1 overlap, or CXMI). A filter model Mctx is fine-tuned to generate that context from query plus passage, and a generator Mgen is fine-tuned to answer from filtered context plus query. At test time Mctx output feeds Mgen.
method.task: retrieval-augmented generation: open-domain QA, multi-hop QA, long-form QA, fact verification, knowledge-grounded dialog

datasets.name: NQ
datasets.source: Kwiatkowski 2019, processed by Lee 2019 (short answers up to 5 tokens)
datasets.preprocessing: passages split into sentences with spaCy

other.used_for: Mctx and Mgen, full fine-tune (inferred: LoRA stated only for LLAMA2)

other.retrieves: top 5 Wikipedia passages; top-1 used in main experiments

training.objective: supervised fine-tuning: Mctx(t_silver | q + P) and Mgen(o | t_silver + q)

other.oracle_selection: single best span; multi-span worse in preliminary studies
other.cxmi_threshold: 0.0 for selection; footnote 4 says 1.0 gave the best results in preliminary studies

inference.max_tokens: Mctx 512; Mgen 128 for extractive QA, fact verification, dialog (other tasks not stated)

metrics.name: unigram precision
metrics.definition: precision of output unigrams w.r.t. context

eval.protocol: single run per setting; KILT tasks reported on dev because test is unavailable; no significance test

results.claim: FILCO cuts model input length by 44-64% across tasks versus full passages.

results.quote: Our method (the FILCO column) effectively reduces input length by 44 −64%.

results.claim: FILCO beats FULL on NQ by +4.3 EM (FLAN-T5) and +8.6 EM (LLAMA2).
results.setup: NQ test, top-1 DPR passage, fine-tuned FLAN-T5 XL 3B and LLAMA2 7B LoRA
results.quote: +4.3 and +8.6 EM increase in NQ with FLAN-T5

results.quote: +6.2 and +4.3 accuracy increase for FEVER with FLAN-

limits: All datasets built from Wikipedia; other domains untested (authors).
Automatic metrics only (EM, unigram F1); no human or neural evaluation (authors).
Filter and generator both need training, though cost is lower than full passages.
Single run, no seeds or variance; optimizer, LoRA settings, hardware not stated.
Main experiments use top-1 passage only; top-5 tested only with FLAN-T5.
Main generation numbers are in Fig 4 only (no table).

terms.definition: binary measure of whether a text span lexically contains the output
conditional cross-mutual information: ratio of generator probability of the output with and without the span

lineage.note: passage-level filtering baseline PSG and EVI.
CXMI score adopted from contextual MT

lineage.work: Large language models can be easily distracted by irrelevant context (Shi et al.)
